Go through every point in each tip box (for example every greeting with its time of day), one or two short sentences each, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: brainstorm (아이디어를 자유롭게 내다), budget (예산), target (목표, 과녁), risk (위험), database (데이터베이스), priority (우선순위), resource (자원), strategy (전략), procedure (절차), technique (기법, 기술), cause (원인), figure ((figure out) 알아내다, 풀다).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. After every two or three words, ask one tiny real question with the word you just did (for example: Are you a morning person?), wait for the answer and react; do this at least twice in this part. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

items: The main issue here is the return step.
The button enables a quick return.
Please ensure the map is clear.
One solution could be a bigger button.
The pop-up had a bad effect.
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: issue ((다뤄야 할) 문제, 사안) — "The main issue here is the return step."; approach (접근 방식, 방법) — "Let’s try a new approach."; lack (부족) — "a lack of time"; enable (가능하게 하다) — "The button enables a quick return."; ensure (반드시 ~하게 하다) — "Please ensure the map is clear."; solution (해결책) — "One solution could be a bigger button."; option (선택지) — "Let’s look at the options."; deadline (마감일) — "The deadline is Friday."; effect (영향, 효과) — "The pop-up had a bad effect."; fix (고치다, 바로잡다) — "How can we fix it?".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Think of a small problem at home, like a slow phone. Name it.
One solution could be ___. / … could be to ___.
Your friend says, “Just buy a new phone.” Answer politely.
That might work. / I’m not sure that would solve it.
How do you usually solve problems, alone or with others?
I usually ___. / I like to brainstorm with ___.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Think of a small problem at home, like a slow phone. Name it." (hint on screen: The problem is that my ___.)
- "Suggest a solution for it." (hint on screen: One solution could be ___. / … could be to ___.)
- "Your friend says, “Just buy a new phone.” Answer politely." (hint on screen: That might work. / I’m not sure that would solve it.)
- "How do you usually solve problems, alone or with others?" (hint on screen: I usually ___. / I like to brainstorm with ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: Think of a small problem at home, like a slow phone. Name it.
Suggest a solution for it.
Your friend says, “Just buy a new phone.” Answer politely.
How do you usually solve problems, alone or with others?

steps.title: Two Quick Versions
steps.text: On Friday, Jiwoo showed two versions. Version A had a big map button, *as opposed to* a button hidden in a menu. Version B used a pop-up. *Prior to* the meeting, she tested both with four coworkers. With A, everyone returned a bike in seconds. B caused a severe problem: the pop-up covered the map, and one person even reversed a step by mistake. “That’s sufficient for now,” said Maya. “Let’s go with A.” But the new button would change the app’s daily *operation*, so they needed *cooperation* from the developers. “We *seek to* eliminate extra steps,” Jiwoo wrote to them. There was no reply *as yet*, but users were *at risk* of giving up if returns went badly. “Let’s *get on with* it,” Maya said.
steps.gloss: as opposed to ~와 달리, ~이 아니라 · prior to ~ 전에 · reverse 되돌리다 · sufficient 충분한 · operation 운영, 돌아가는 방식 · seek to ~하려고 하다 · eliminate 없애다 · at risk 위험에 처한
questions: What was the problem with Version B?
Why did they need help from the developers?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Two Quick Versions". Text: "On Friday, Jiwoo showed two versions. Version A had a big map button, as opposed to a button hidden in a menu. Version B used a pop-up. Prior to the meeting, she tested both with four coworkers. With A, everyone returned a bike in seconds. B caused a severe problem: the pop-up covered the map, and one person even reversed a step by mistake. “That’s sufficient for now,” said Maya. “Let’s go with A.” But the new button would change the app’s daily operation, so they needed cooperation from the developers. “We seek to eliminate extra steps,” Jiwoo wrote to them. There was no reply as yet, but users were at risk of giving up if returns went badly. “Let’s get on with it,” Maya said." Words: as opposed to ~와 달리, ~이 아니라 · prior to ~ 전에 · reverse 되돌리다 · sufficient 충분한 · operation 운영, 돌아가는 방식 · seek to ~하려고 하다 · eliminate 없애다 · at risk 위험에 처한.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What was the problem with Version B?" / "Why did they need help from the developers?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘The problem is that ___.’로 문제를 분명하게 말할 수 있어요.
‘One solution could be ___.’로 해결책을 부드럽게 제안할 수 있어요.
‘That might work.’나 ‘I’m not sure that would solve it.’으로 아이디어에 답할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘The problem is that ___.’로 문제를 분명하게 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘One solution could be ___.’로 해결책을 부드럽게 제안할 수 있어요.
- ‘That might work.’나 ‘I’m not sure that would solve it.’으로 아이디어에 답할 수 있어요.
First ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence, and stop there to wait. React and praise specifically. Only then, in a later turn, end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

lessons.title: 제안하고 설득하기
lessons.goal: 강하게 제안하고, 좋은 결과를 들어 설득하고, 받아들이기

steps.title: 제안하고 설득하기
steps.goal: 강하게 제안하고, 좋은 결과를 들어 설득하고, 받아들이기
steps.scene_desc: 11월 말 오후, 사무실 창가. 지우가 태블릿에 그린 큰 지도 버튼 스케치를 마야에게 보여 주며 손짓으로 열심히 설명하고, 마야가 커피잔을 든 채 창가에 기대어 생각하는 얼굴로 듣고 있음. 창밖은 늦가을 도시 풍경(화면·간판에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat, one question per turn: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally. The warm-up is long enough only when the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions (one is enough if your class notes say you already had a class with them today); do not mention today's topic or ask if they are ready before that.
2) Then, in a new turn, bring up today's topic in your own words: "It would save time." (제안하고 설득하기). Goal: 강하게 제안하고, 좋은 결과를 들어 설득하고, 받아들이기. Today's scene: 11월 말 오후, 사무실 창가. 지우가 태블릿에 그린 큰 지도 버튼 스케치를 마야에게 보여 주며 손짓으로 열심히 설명하고, 마야가 커피잔을 든 채 창가에 기대어 생각하는 얼굴로 듣고 있음. 창밖은 늦가을 도시 풍경. People in the scene (say the names exactly like this): Jiwoo, Maya. Say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above). Bring up the topic only once and ask if they are ready only once. When the learner says they are ready, answer with one short, warm sentence like a person would (for example: Great, let's start.) and nothing more.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "I really think we should ___.".

steps.when: 강하게 제안할 때 써요. *really*를 넣으면 확신이 실려요. should 뒤에는 동사원형.
steps.extra: I really think we should change the return screen.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "I really think we should ___." (꼭 ~하는 게 좋겠어요.). When to use it: 강하게 제안할 때 써요. really를 넣으면 확신이 실려요. should 뒤에는 동사원형. Note: I really think we should change the return screen.
Teach it like a person, in three small turns. One thing per turn, and wait for the learner each time. Never name these turns or say what kind of practice comes next; just talk:
(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) The learner says it with their own real word in the blank (for example their own name). Show it first with your own real word; nobody ever says the blank itself. Any word of theirs that makes a correct sentence is right, even when the book uses another one.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It would ___.".

steps.when: 아이디어대로 했을 때 생길 결과를 말해요. *would* + 동사원형.
steps.extra: It would save time. · It would make returns easier.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "It would ___." ((그러면) ~할 거예요.). When to use it: 아이디어대로 했을 때 생길 결과를 말해요. would + 동사원형. Note: It would save time. · It would make returns easier.
Teach it like a person, in three small turns. One thing per turn, and wait for the learner each time. Never name these turns or say what kind of practice comes next; just talk:
(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) The learner says it with their own real word in the blank (for example their own name). Show it first with your own real word; nobody ever says the blank itself. Any word of theirs that makes a correct sentence is right, even when the book uses another one.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Let’s give it a try.".

steps.when: 100% 확신은 없어도 제안을 받아들일 때 써요.
steps.extra: OK, you’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a try.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Let’s give it a try." (한번 해 봐요.). When to use it: 100% 확신은 없어도 제안을 받아들일 때 써요. Note: OK, you’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a try.
Teach it like a person, in three small turns. One thing per turn, and wait for the learner each time. Never name these turns or say what kind of practice comes next; just talk:
(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) Give a different everyday moment where they need it, and let them say it there.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Hear Me Out · 11월 말 오후, 사무실 창가에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Hear Me Out · 11월 말 오후, 사무실 창가에서

lines.en: Maya, do you have a minute? I have a proposal for the return screen.
lines.ko: 마야, 잠깐 시간 있어요? 반납 화면에 대해 제안할 게 있어요.

lines.en: Sure. Go ahead.
lines.ko: 그럼요. 말해 봐요.

lines.en: Right now, returning a bike takes three screens. {{I really think we should}} make it one screen, with the big map button.
lines.ko: 지금은 자전거를 반납하려면 화면을 세 개 거쳐야 해요. 큰 지도 버튼을 넣어서 꼭 한 화면으로 줄이는 게 좋겠어요.

lines.en: Hmm. The developers are busy, and the Vancouver team designed those screens.
lines.ko: 음. 개발자들이 바쁘고, 그 화면들은 밴쿠버 팀이 디자인했잖아요.

lines.en: Hear me out. {{It would}} save users a lot of time. In our test, it took almost a minute.
lines.ko: 끝까지 들어 봐요. 그러면 사용자들 시간이 많이 절약될 거예요. 저희 테스트에서는 거의 1분이 걸렸어요.

lines.en: And with one screen?
lines.ko: 한 화면이면요?

lines.en: About ten seconds. Think about it this way. Imagine if you were late for work and couldn’t return your bike.
lines.ko: 10초쯤이요. 이렇게 생각해 봐요. 출근이 늦었는데 자전거를 반납할 수 없다고 상상해 봐요.

lines.en: I’d be pretty annoyed.
lines.ko: 꽤 짜증 나겠죠.

lines.en: Exactly. It would also mean fewer calls to the help center. What do we have to lose?
lines.ko: 바로 그거예요. 고객센터로 오는 전화도 줄어들 거고요. 손해 볼 게 뭐 있어요?

lines.en: Well… it would save us a lot of time later, too. OK, you’ve convinced me. {{Let’s give it a try.}}
lines.ko: 음… 나중에 우리 시간도 많이 아껴 주겠네요. 좋아요, 설득됐어요. 한번 해 봐요.

lines.en: Thank you! The Vancouver team should see it, too. Maybe at my presentation in January?
lines.ko: 고마워요! 밴쿠버 팀도 봐야 해요. 1월 제 발표 때 보여 주면 어떨까요?

lines.en: Fair point, let’s do it.
lines.ko: 좋은 지적이에요, 그렇게 해요.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Hear Me Out · 11월 말 오후, 사무실 창가에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Jiwoo: "Maya, do you have a minute? I have a proposal for the return screen." (마야, 잠깐 시간 있어요? 반납 화면에 대해 제안할 게 있어요.)
2. Maya: "Sure. Go ahead." (그럼요. 말해 봐요.)
3. Jiwoo: "Right now, returning a bike takes three screens. I really think we should make it one screen, with the big map button." (지금은 자전거를 반납하려면 화면을 세 개 거쳐야 해요. 큰 지도 버튼을 넣어서 꼭 한 화면으로 줄이는 게 좋겠어요.)
4. Maya: "Hmm. The developers are busy, and the Vancouver team designed those screens." (음. 개발자들이 바쁘고, 그 화면들은 밴쿠버 팀이 디자인했잖아요.)
5. Jiwoo: "Hear me out. It would save users a lot of time. In our test, it took almost a minute." (끝까지 들어 봐요. 그러면 사용자들 시간이 많이 절약될 거예요. 저희 테스트에서는 거의 1분이 걸렸어요.)
6. Maya: "And with one screen?" (한 화면이면요?)
7. Jiwoo: "About ten seconds. Think about it this way. Imagine if you were late for work and couldn’t return your bike." (10초쯤이요. 이렇게 생각해 봐요. 출근이 늦었는데 자전거를 반납할 수 없다고 상상해 봐요.)
8. Maya: "I’d be pretty annoyed." (꽤 짜증 나겠죠.)
9. Jiwoo: "Exactly. It would also mean fewer calls to the help center. What do we have to lose?" (바로 그거예요. 고객센터로 오는 전화도 줄어들 거고요. 손해 볼 게 뭐 있어요?)
10. Maya: "Well… it would save us a lot of time later, too. OK, you’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a try." (음… 나중에 우리 시간도 많이 아껴 주겠네요. 좋아요, 설득됐어요. 한번 해 봐요.)
11. Jiwoo: "Thank you! The Vancouver team should see it, too. Maybe at my presentation in January?" (고마워요! 밴쿠버 팀도 봐야 해요. 1월 제 발표 때 보여 주면 어떨까요?)
12. Maya: "Fair point, let’s do it." (좋은 지적이에요, 그렇게 해요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. The learner plays Jiwoo in this lesson, so an answer in the first person (I'm new here instead of Jiwoo is new here) is right too; never correct that. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Maya exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Jiwoo (learner): "Maya, do you have a minute? I have a proposal for the return screen." (마야, 잠깐 시간 있어요? 반납 화면에 대해 제안할 게 있어요.)
2. Maya (you): "Sure. Go ahead." (그럼요. 말해 봐요.)
3. Jiwoo (learner): "Right now, returning a bike takes three screens. I really think we should make it one screen, with the big map button." (지금은 자전거를 반납하려면 화면을 세 개 거쳐야 해요. 큰 지도 버튼을 넣어서 꼭 한 화면으로 줄이는 게 좋겠어요.)
4. Maya (you): "Hmm. The developers are busy, and the Vancouver team designed those screens." (음. 개발자들이 바쁘고, 그 화면들은 밴쿠버 팀이 디자인했잖아요.)
5. Jiwoo (learner): "Hear me out. It would save users a lot of time. In our test, it took almost a minute." (끝까지 들어 봐요. 그러면 사용자들 시간이 많이 절약될 거예요. 저희 테스트에서는 거의 1분이 걸렸어요.)
6. Maya (you): "And with one screen?" (한 화면이면요?)
7. Jiwoo (learner): "About ten seconds. Think about it this way. Imagine if you were late for work and couldn’t return your bike." (10초쯤이요. 이렇게 생각해 봐요. 출근이 늦었는데 자전거를 반납할 수 없다고 상상해 봐요.)
8. Maya (you): "I’d be pretty annoyed." (꽤 짜증 나겠죠.)
9. Jiwoo (learner): "Exactly. It would also mean fewer calls to the help center. What do we have to lose?" (바로 그거예요. 고객센터로 오는 전화도 줄어들 거고요. 손해 볼 게 뭐 있어요?)
10. Maya (you): "Well… it would save us a lot of time later, too. OK, you’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a try." (음… 나중에 우리 시간도 많이 아껴 주겠네요. 좋아요, 설득됐어요. 한번 해 봐요.)
11. Jiwoo (learner): "Thank you! The Vancouver team should see it, too. Maybe at my presentation in January?" (고마워요! 밴쿠버 팀도 봐야 해요. 1월 제 발표 때 보여 주면 어떨까요?)
12. Maya (you): "Fair point, let’s do it." (좋은 지적이에요, 그렇게 해요.)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Maya. The learner speaks first: call highlight_line with 1 and invite them to start. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say most of it or a good part of a long line, accept it warmly and go on; only if what they say is clearly not their line, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

items: Right now, returning a bike takes three screens.
Maya agrees with Jiwoo right away.
Jiwoo will show the new screen at her presentation in January.

1. Right now, returning a bike takes three screens. → True (line 3)
2. Maya agrees with Jiwoo right away. → False (line 4, 10)
3. Jiwoo will show the new screen at her presentation in January. → either answer can be defended: accept the learner's answer and say in a few words what the lines say

Go by the answers above, not by what the learner says: if their answer is the other one, say so kindly and show the line. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. Give the verdict in the language you are using with this learner. Only when you are speaking Korean to them, say it as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: It would ___. / Let’s give it a try.
head: 제안 (I really think we should …)
결과 (It would …)
대답
rows: It would give us more time.
It would show the real problem.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key sentences: I really think we should ___. / It would ___. / Let’s give it a try. Table (제안 (I really think we should …) → 결과 (It would …)):
- make it one screen. → It would save time.
- start meetings earlier. → It would give us more time.
- add a dark mode. → It would help at night.
- ask users first. → It would show the real problem.
Make three quick real-life moments out of the key sentences and the rows, one per turn (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. If their sentence is correct and natural, accept it even when the table uses other words. Do not read labels or arrows aloud, and never say a blank: use real words. This part is finished only when the learner has answered three of these moments. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
If we made it one screen, it *would save* time. 한 화면으로 줄이면 시간이 절약될 거예요. 
짧게: It *would* save time. · It*’d* be easier. (would + 동사원형)

*Imagine if* you *were* late for work. 출근이 늦었다고 상상해 봐요(가정한 상황). 
will = 예측·예상되는 결과 · would = 상상한 상황의 결과
errors: I really think we should to try it.
I really think we should try it.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- would — 아이디어의 결과: If we made it one screen, it would save time. 한 화면으로 줄이면 시간이 절약될 거예요. / 짧게: It would save time. · It’d be easier. (would + 동사원형)
- Imagine if + 과거형: Imagine if you were late for work. 출근이 늦었다고 상상해 봐요(가정한 상황). / will = 예측·예상되는 결과 · would = 상상한 상황의 결과
Common mistakes on screen:
- It would saves time. → It would save time. (would 뒤에는 동사원형.)
- I really think we should to try it. → I really think we should try it. (should 뒤에 to를 쓰지 않아요.)
- Let’s give a try it. → Let’s give it a try. (give it a try 순서로.)
There are 2 grammar points and 3 mistakes. Go through them as a conversation, one new thing per turn, never as a lecture. Start with the first point right away, with no opening sentence about how you will do this:
- Each grammar point: say its main idea in one or two plain, easy sentences with one short example with real words (do not go through every detail of the point), then ask the learner to make one short sentence of their own with it. When they answer, react to their sentence in a few words, and go on to the next thing in the same reply.
- Then the mistakes, one at a time: say the wrong sentence and ask the learner to fix it. When they answer, first confirm the right sentence and say why in a few words, then give the next wrong sentence in the same reply. Do every mistake on screen this way.
Never give two new points or two new mistakes in one turn, and never skip the confirmation. After the last mistake is fixed and confirmed, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: would — 아이디어의 결과: If we made it one screen, it would save time. 한 화면으로 줄이면 시간이 절약될 거예요. 짧게: It would save time. · It’d be easier. (would + 동사원형)
Imagine if + 과거형: Imagine if you were late for work. 출근이 늦었다고 상상해 봐요(가정한 상황). will = 예측·예상되는 결과 · would = 상상한 상황의 결과
mistakes: It would saves time. → It would save time.
I really think we should to try it. → I really think we should try it.
Let’s give a try it. → Let’s give it a try.

steps.note: 예) make it one screen / save time → I really think we should make it one screen. It would save time. — OK, let’s give it a try.
steps.teach:
Quick practice. How it works (written on the learner's screen; do not read it out): 예) make it one screen / save time → I really think we should make it one screen. It would save time. — OK, let’s give it a try. The items (the words the learner gets for each one): make it one screen / save time | start meetings earlier / give us more time | add a dark mode / help at night | ask users first / show the real problem.
The sample on screen shows what is said for one item and who says it (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes it is a two-person exchange). If the sample has a dash (—), the words before the dash are one speaker and the words after it are the other: split it like a real conversation, the learner says one side and you say the other. The learner should get to use the given words. If both words belong to one side, the learner says that side and you say the other. If the words are split between the two sides (for example a question with the first word and an answer with the second), take turns across the items: for one item you ask and the learner answers with the second word, for the next the learner asks with the first word and you answer. When you set up an item, say which side the learner takes and give them only the word that goes into it. Never make the learner say both sides in one go. If their sentence is correct English and uses the given word, it is right: say so and go on, and never ask for extra words from the sample. Do not say the sample or the answer before the learner tries: from the first item they build it themselves. Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear, in different words each time, let the learner answer, and react like a person. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "It would save time." (제안하고 설득하기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "I really think we should ___." / "It would ___." / "Let’s give it a try.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: It would save us a lot of time.
What do we have to lose?
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 주의 끌기: "Hear me out." (제 말 끝까지 들어 봐요., 친근); "Think about it this way." (이렇게 생각해 봐요., 보통); "Imagine if ___." (~라고 상상해 봐요., 보통)
- 설득하기: "It would save us a lot of time." (시간이 많이 절약될 거예요., 보통); "What do we have to lose?" (손해 볼 게 뭐 있어요?, 친근); "Trust me on this." (이건 저를 믿어 봐요., 친근)
- 받아들이기: "You’ve convinced me." (설득됐어요., 보통); "I’m on board." (저도 찬성이에요., 친근); "Fair point, let’s do it." (좋은 지적이에요, 그렇게 해요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 설득할 때 쓰는 낱말

*persuade* someone 설득하다 · *argue* that … (이유를 들어) 주장하다 
*appeal* to users 사용자의 마음을 끌다 · *promote* a feature 기능을 홍보하다 
a marketing *campaign* 마케팅 캠페인 · *force* users to scroll 억지로 스크롤하게 하다
격식 있는 표현 (참고)

It could *give rise to* new problems. 새 문제를 낳을 수 있어요(격식). 
*pick out* the best idea 가장 좋은 아이디어를 고르다 · a *mere* ten seconds 겨우 10초 
이 이야기의 테스트 숫자는 지어낸 거예요.
steps.blank:
A: I really think we ___ make it one screen. It ___ save time. 
B: Hmm. I’m not sure.   A: Hear me ___. What do we have to ___? 
B: OK, you’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a ___. 
낱말 상자: should · would · out · lose · try
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 설득할 때 쓰는 낱말: persuade someone 설득하다 · argue that … (이유를 들어) 주장하다 / appeal to users 사용자의 마음을 끌다 · promote a feature 기능을 홍보하다 / a marketing campaign 마케팅 캠페인 · force users to scroll 억지로 스크롤하게 하다
- 격식 있는 표현 (참고): It could give rise to new problems. 새 문제를 낳을 수 있어요(격식). / pick out the best idea 가장 좋은 아이디어를 고르다 · a mere ten seconds 겨우 10초 / 이 이야기의 테스트 숫자는 지어낸 거예요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: I really think we ___ make it one screen. It ___ save time. / B: Hmm. I’m not sure. A: Hear me ___. What do we have to ___? / B: OK, you’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a ___. / 낱말 상자: should · would · out · lose · try
Go through every point in each tip box (for example every greeting with its time of day), one or two short sentences each, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: proposal (제안, 제안서), propose (제안하다), persuade (설득하다), argue ((이유를 들어) 주장하다), result (결과), gain (얻다; 늘다), force (억지로 ~하게 하다), campaign (캠페인, (목표를 위한) 활동), promote (홍보하다), supporter (지지자), appeal ((마음을) 끌다), efficient (효율적인).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. After every two or three words, ask one tiny real question with the word you just did (for example: Are you a morning person?), wait for the answer and react; do this at least twice in this part. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

items: The big button is very effective.
It would save us a lot of time.
What do we have to lose?
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: effective (효과적인) — "The big button is very effective."; convince (설득하다, 믿게 하다) — "You’ve convinced me."; suggest (제안하다) — "I suggest a new screen."; benefit (이점, 좋은 점) — "The main benefit is speed."; save ((시간·돈을) 아끼다, 절약하다) — "It would save us a lot of time."; lose (잃다; 손해 보다) — "What do we have to lose?"; trust (믿다, 신뢰하다) — "Trust me on this."; worth (~할 가치가 있는) — "It’s worth a try."; support (지지하다, 밀어주다(앞에서는 ‘뒷받침하다’)) — "The team supports the idea.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Think of a change for your club, class, or team. Suggest it strongly.
What good result would it have?
Your friend says, “Hear me out. Let’s study every morning.” Answer.
You’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a try.
Have you ever persuaded someone to try something new?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Think of a change for your club, class, or team. Suggest it strongly." (hint on screen: I really think we should ___.)
- "What good result would it have?" (hint on screen: It would ___.)
- "Your friend says, “Hear me out. Let’s study every morning.” Answer." (hint on screen: You’ve convinced me. Let’s give it a try.)
- "Have you ever persuaded someone to try something new?" (hint on screen: Yes, I persuaded my ___ to ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: Think of a change for your club, class, or team. Suggest it strongly.
What good result would it have?
Your friend says, “Hear me out. Let’s study every morning.” Answer.
Have you ever persuaded someone to try something new?

steps.title: The One-Step Return
steps.text: Over the next week, Jiwoo *picked out* the best ideas from the test. The new screen works *as follows*: tap the big map button, check the station, and you’re done. *In effect*, three screens become one. In her notes, Jiwoo argued that slow returns *result in* angry users, and that a *mere* ten seconds would make a dramatic difference. “We’ll need to integrate it with the payment step,” Maya said. “Will that *give rise to* new problems? *If so*, we’ll fix them.” The developers agreed to undertake the work in December. Ultimately, the team hopes to convert first-time riders into regular users and sustain that growth. In January, Jiwoo would show the new screen to the Vancouver team.
steps.gloss: pick out 고르다 · as follows 다음과 같이 · in effect 사실상 · result in ~로 이어지다, ~을 낳다 · mere 겨우 ~의 · integrate 통합하다, 합치다 · undertake (일을) 맡아 하다 · convert 바꾸다, 전환하다 · sustain 유지하다, 이어 가다
questions: How does the new screen work?
When will the developers do the work?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "The One-Step Return". Text: "Over the next week, Jiwoo picked out the best ideas from the test. The new screen works as follows: tap the big map button, check the station, and you’re done. In effect, three screens become one. In her notes, Jiwoo argued that slow returns result in angry users, and that a mere ten seconds would make a dramatic difference. “We’ll need to integrate it with the payment step,” Maya said. “Will that give rise to new problems? If so, we’ll fix them.” The developers agreed to undertake the work in December. Ultimately, the team hopes to convert first-time riders into regular users and sustain that growth. In January, Jiwoo would show the new screen to the Vancouver team." Words: pick out 고르다 · as follows 다음과 같이 · in effect 사실상 · result in ~로 이어지다, ~을 낳다 · mere 겨우 ~의 · integrate 통합하다, 합치다 · undertake (일을) 맡아 하다 · convert 바꾸다, 전환하다 · sustain 유지하다, 이어 가다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "How does the new screen work?" / "When will the developers do the work?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘I really think we should ___.’로 강하게 제안할 수 있어요.
‘It would ___.’로 아이디어의 좋은 결과를 말할 수 있어요.
‘Let’s give it a try.’나 ‘I’m on board.’로 제안을 받아들일 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘I really think we should ___.’로 강하게 제안할 수 있어요.
- ‘It would ___.’로 아이디어의 좋은 결과를 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘Let’s give it a try.’나 ‘I’m on board.’로 제안을 받아들일 수 있어요.
First ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence, and stop there to wait. React and praise specifically. Only then, in a later turn, end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

lessons.title: 조건 맞추기

steps.title: 조건 맞추기
steps.goal: 조건을 걸고 협상해 중간에서 합의하기
steps.scene_desc: 12월 초 오후, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 대니얼이 노트에 숫자를 적어 지우 쪽으로 밀며 웃고, 지우가 손가락 하나를 들어 조건을 말함. 탁자 위에 커피 두 잔과 쿠키 접시, 창밖에는 첫눈이 살짝 내리는 거리(화면·노트·간판에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat, one question per turn: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally. The warm-up is long enough only when the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions (one is enough if your class notes say you already had a class with them today); do not mention today's topic or ask if they are ready before that.
2) Then, in a new turn, bring up today's topic in your own words: "Let’s meet halfway." (조건 맞추기). Goal: 조건을 걸고 협상해 중간에서 합의하기. Today's scene: 12월 초 오후, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 대니얼이 노트에 숫자를 적어 지우 쪽으로 밀며 웃고, 지우가 손가락 하나를 들어 조건을 말함. 탁자 위에 커피 두 잔과 쿠키 접시, 창밖에는 첫눈이 살짝 내리는 거리. People in the scene (say the names exactly like this): Daniel, Jiwoo. Say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above). Bring up the topic only once and ask if they are ready only once. When the learner says they are ready, answer with one short, warm sentence like a person would (for example: Great, let's start.) and nothing more.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Would you be willing to ___?".

steps.when: 상대가 조건을 받아들여 줄 수 있는지 정중하게 물어요. *to* 뒤에는 동사원형.
steps.extra: Would you be willing to share the results?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Would you be willing to ___?" (~해 주실 수 있을까요?). When to use it: 상대가 조건을 받아들여 줄 수 있는지 정중하게 물어요. to 뒤에는 동사원형. Note: Would you be willing to share the results?
Teach it like a person, in three small turns. One thing per turn, and wait for the learner each time. Never name these turns or say what kind of practice comes next; just talk:
(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) The learner says it with their own real word in the blank (for example their own name). Show it first with your own real word; nobody ever says the blank itself. Any word of theirs that makes a correct sentence is right, even when the book uses another one.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "If you can ___, we could ___.".

steps.when: 조건을 걸고 거래를 제안해요. 내 조건을 먼저, 해 줄 수 있는 것을 뒤에 말해요.
steps.extra: If you can keep it short, we could send it to our users.
steps.teach:

(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) The learner says it with their own real word in the blank (for example their own name). Show it first with your own real word; nobody ever says the blank itself. Any word of theirs that makes a correct sentence is right, even when the book uses another one.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Let’s meet halfway.".

steps.when: 원하는 것이 서로 다를 때 중간 지점을 제안해요.
steps.extra: You want 20 and I want 10. Let’s meet halfway. How about 15?

Teach it like a person, in three small turns. One thing per turn, and wait for the learner each time. Never name these turns or say what kind of practice comes next; just talk:
(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) Give a different everyday moment where they need it, and let them say it there.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("A Fair Deal · 12월 초, 동네 카페에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: A Fair Deal · 12월 초, 동네 카페에서

lines.en: Jiwoo, my lab wants to do a survey on how people use shared bikes. {{Would you be willing to}} send it to your app users? It’s twenty questions, and we need a minimum of five hundred answers by December 20.
lines.ko: 지우, 저희 연구실에서 사람들이 공유 자전거를 어떻게 쓰는지 설문하려고 해요. 앱 사용자들에게 보내 줄래요? 질문 20개, 12월 20일까지 최소 500명이 답해야 해요.

lines.en: Twenty is too many. Most of our users stop after ten.
lines.ko: 스무 개는 너무 많아요. 저희 사용자 대부분은 열 개쯤 하고 그만둬요.

lines.en: Really? What’s your evidence?
lines.ko: 정말요? 근거가 뭐예요?

lines.en: Our last in-app survey. Most people quit around question ten. So ten is our maximum.
lines.ko: 지난번 앱 안 설문이요. 대부분 10번 질문쯤에서 그만뒀어요. 그래서 열 개가 최대예요.

lines.en: Ten is too few for us. {{Let’s meet halfway}}. Fifteen? We can’t go any lower.
lines.ko: 열 개는 저희한테 너무 적어요. 서로 조금씩 양보해요. 열다섯 개 어때요? 더는 못 줄여요.

lines.en: OK, fifteen. Is there any room for negotiation on the deadline? December is busy for us.
lines.ko: 좋아요, 열다섯 개. 마감일은 조정할 여지가 있을까요? 12월은 저희가 바빠서요.

lines.en: Mid-January? That’s our best offer.
lines.ko: 1월 중순은요? 그게 저희가 해 드릴 수 있는 최선이에요.

lines.en: Good. And {{if you can}} share the results with us first, {{we could}} send the survey to all our users.
lines.ko: 좋아요. 그리고 결과를 저희와 먼저 공유해 주시면, 설문을 전체 사용자에게 보낼 수 있어요.

lines.en: That’s a deal! For the participants, maybe a small gift card?
lines.ko: 좋아요, 그렇게 하죠! 참여자들한테는 작은 기프트 카드를 줄까요?

lines.en: What if we offered a free ride instead? But I’ll need to run it by my boss first.
lines.ko: 대신 무료 이용권을 주면 어때요? 그래도 먼저 상사한테 물어봐야 해요.

lines.en: Of course. We’re almost there. Then let’s put that in writing.
lines.ko: 물론이죠. 거의 다 합의했네요. 그럼 그 내용을 글로 남겨 둬요.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "A Fair Deal · 12월 초, 동네 카페에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Daniel: "Jiwoo, my lab wants to do a survey on how people use shared bikes. Would you be willing to send it to your app users? It’s twenty questions, and we need a minimum of five hundred answers by December 20." (지우, 저희 연구실에서 사람들이 공유 자전거를 어떻게 쓰는지 설문하려고 해요. 앱 사용자들에게 보내 줄래요? 질문 20개, 12월 20일까지 최소 500명이 답해야 해요.)
2. Jiwoo: "Twenty is too many. Most of our users stop after ten." (스무 개는 너무 많아요. 저희 사용자 대부분은 열 개쯤 하고 그만둬요.)
3. Daniel: "Really? What’s your evidence?" (정말요? 근거가 뭐예요?)
4. Jiwoo: "Our last in-app survey. Most people quit around question ten. So ten is our maximum." (지난번 앱 안 설문이요. 대부분 10번 질문쯤에서 그만뒀어요. 그래서 열 개가 최대예요.)
5. Daniel: "Ten is too few for us. Let’s meet halfway. Fifteen? We can’t go any lower." (열 개는 저희한테 너무 적어요. 서로 조금씩 양보해요. 열다섯 개 어때요? 더는 못 줄여요.)
6. Jiwoo: "OK, fifteen. Is there any room for negotiation on the deadline? December is busy for us." (좋아요, 열다섯 개. 마감일은 조정할 여지가 있을까요? 12월은 저희가 바빠서요.)
7. Daniel: "Mid-January? That’s our best offer." (1월 중순은요? 그게 저희가 해 드릴 수 있는 최선이에요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Good. And if you can share the results with us first, we could send the survey to all our users." (좋아요. 그리고 결과를 저희와 먼저 공유해 주시면, 설문을 전체 사용자에게 보낼 수 있어요.)
9. Daniel: "That’s a deal! For the participants, maybe a small gift card?" (좋아요, 그렇게 하죠! 참여자들한테는 작은 기프트 카드를 줄까요?)
10. Jiwoo: "What if we offered a free ride instead? But I’ll need to run it by my boss first." (대신 무료 이용권을 주면 어때요? 그래도 먼저 상사한테 물어봐야 해요.)
11. Daniel: "Of course. We’re almost there. Then let’s put that in writing." (물론이죠. 거의 다 합의했네요. 그럼 그 내용을 글로 남겨 둬요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. The learner plays Jiwoo in this lesson, so an answer in the first person (I'm new here instead of Jiwoo is new here) is right too; never correct that. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

8. Jiwoo: "Good. And if you can share the results with us first, we could send the survey to all our users." (좋아요. 그리고 결과를 저희와 먼저 공유해 주시면, 설문을 전체 사용자에게 보낼 수 있어요.)
9. Daniel: "That’s a deal! For the participants, maybe a small gift card?" (좋아요, 그렇게 하죠! 참여자들한테는 작은 기프트 카드를 줄까요?)
10. Jiwoo: "What if we offered a free ride instead? But I’ll need to run it by my boss first." (대신 무료 이용권을 주면 어때요? 그래도 먼저 상사한테 물어봐야 해요.)
11. Daniel: "Of course. We’re almost there. Then let’s put that in writing." (물론이죠. 거의 다 합의했네요. 그럼 그 내용을 글로 남겨 둬요.)
Go by the answers above, not by what the learner says: if their answer is the other one, say so kindly and show the line. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. Give the verdict in the language you are using with this learner. Only when you are speaking Korean to them, say it as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: If you can ___, we could ___. / Let’s meet halfway.
head: 조건 (If you can …)
해 줄 수 있는 것 (we could …)
대답
rows: send it to all our users.
I’ll need to run it by my boss.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key sentences: Would you be willing to ___? / If you can ___, we could ___. / Let’s meet halfway. Table (조건 (If you can …) → 해 줄 수 있는 것 (we could …)):
- share the results first, → send it to all our users.
- finish by Friday, → pay a little more.
- keep it short, → start next week.
- order more bikes, → give you a discount.
Make three quick real-life moments out of the key sentences and the rows, one per turn (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. If their sentence is correct and natural, accept it even when the table uses other words. Do not read labels or arrows aloud, and never say a blank: use real words. This part is finished only when the learner has answered three of these moments. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items: If you can …, we could … — 조건을 건 제안

*Would you be willing to* wait until January? 1월까지 기다려 주실 수 있을까요? (to + 동사원형) 
대답: Yes, I’d be willing to do that. · I’m afraid not.
errors: If you can waiting, we could pay more.
If you can wait, we could pay more.
Would you be willing to waiting?
Would you be willing to wait?
Is there any room for negotiate?
Is there any room for negotiation?
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- If you can …, we could … — 조건을 건 제안: If you can share the results, we could send it. 결과를 공유해 주시면, 저희가 보낼 수 있어요. / if + can (내 조건) → could (해 줄 수 있는 것) / 비교: If I were you, I’d … (상상한 상황)
- Would you be willing to …?: Would you be willing to wait until January? 1월까지 기다려 주실 수 있을까요? (to + 동사원형) / 대답: Yes, I’d be willing to do that. · I’m afraid not.
Common mistakes on screen:
- If you can waiting, we could pay more. → If you can wait, we could pay more. (can 뒤에는 동사원형.)
- Would you be willing to waiting? → Would you be willing to wait? (to 뒤에는 동사원형.)
- Is there any room for negotiate? → Is there any room for negotiation? (for 뒤에는 명사(negotiation).)
There are 2 grammar points and 3 mistakes. Go through them as a conversation, one new thing per turn, never as a lecture. Start with the first point right away, with no opening sentence about how you will do this:
- Each grammar point: say its main idea in one or two plain, easy sentences with one short example with real words (do not go through every detail of the point), then ask the learner to make one short sentence of their own with it. When they answer, react to their sentence in a few words, and go on to the next thing in the same reply.
- Then the mistakes, one at a time: say the wrong sentence and ask the learner to fix it. When they answer, first confirm the right sentence and say why in a few words, then give the next wrong sentence in the same reply. Do every mistake on screen this way.
Never give two new points or two new mistakes in one turn, and never skip the confirmation. After the last mistake is fixed and confirmed, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: If you can …, we could … — 조건을 건 제안: If you can share the results, we could send it. 결과를 공유해 주시면, 저희가 보낼 수 있어요. if + can (내 조건) → could (해 줄 수 있는 것) 비교: If I were you, I’d … (상상한 상황)
Would you be willing to …?: Would you be willing to wait until January? 1월까지 기다려 주실 수 있을까요? (to + 동사원형) 대답: Yes, I’d be willing to do that. · I’m afraid not.
mistakes: If you can waiting, we could pay more. → If you can wait, we could pay more.
Would you be willing to waiting? → Would you be willing to wait?
Is there any room for negotiate? → Is there any room for negotiation?

steps.note: 예) share the results / send it to all our users → If you can share the results, we could send it to all our users. — That’s a deal.
items: send it to all our users
steps.teach:
Quick practice. How it works (written on the learner's screen; do not read it out): 예) share the results / send it to all our users → If you can share the results, we could send it to all our users. — That’s a deal. The items (the words the learner gets for each one): share the results / send it to all our users | finish by Friday / pay a little more | keep it short / start next week | order more bikes / give you a discount.
The sample on screen shows what is said for one item and who says it (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes it is a two-person exchange). If the sample has a dash (—), the words before the dash are one speaker and the words after it are the other: split it like a real conversation, the learner says one side and you say the other. The learner should get to use the given words. If both words belong to one side, the learner says that side and you say the other. If the words are split between the two sides (for example a question with the first word and an answer with the second), take turns across the items: for one item you ask and the learner answers with the second word, for the next the learner asks with the first word and you answer. When you set up an item, say which side the learner takes and give them only the word that goes into it. Never make the learner say both sides in one go. If their sentence is correct English and uses the given word, it is right: say so and go on, and never ask for extra words from the sample. Do not say the sample or the answer before the learner tries: from the first item they build it themselves. Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear, in different words each time, let the learner answer, and react like a person. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Let’s meet halfway." (조건 맞추기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Would you be willing to ___?" / "If you can ___, we could ___." / "Let’s meet halfway.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: 그게 저희가 드릴 수 있는 최선이에요.
Is there any room for negotiation?
I’ll need to run it by my boss.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 조건 제시하기: "That’s our best offer." (그게 저희가 드릴 수 있는 최선이에요., 정중); "We can’t go any lower." (더는 못 낮춰요., 보통); "Is there any room for negotiation?" (조정할 여지가 있을까요?, 정중)
- 중간 지점 찾기: "What if we ___ instead?" (대신 ~하면 어때요?, 보통); "We’re almost there." (거의 다 합의했어요., 친근); "Can we agree on that?" (그걸로 합의할까요?, 보통)
- 거래 마무리하기: "That’s a deal." (좋아요, 그렇게 해요., 친근); "I’ll need to run it by my boss." (상사한테 먼저 물어봐야 해요., 보통); "Let’s put that in writing." (그 내용을 글로 남겨 둬요., 정중)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 들어 두면 좋은 비즈니스 낱말 (참고)

a *supplier* 공급 업체(회사에 부품을 파는 곳) · a bike *dealer* 자전거 판매상 
a *competitor* · a *rival* 같은 시장의 경쟁 회사, 경쟁자 
a *bid* 입찰(일을 따내려고 내는 가격) · an *acquisition* (회사) 인수 
a *shareholder* 주주 · a *dispute* 분쟁, 의견 다툼
표현 더 보기 (참고)

There’s no magic *formula*. 딱 맞는 공식은 없어요. 
The answers are *dependent* on the weather. 응답은 날씨에 따라 달라요. 
대니얼의 연구실과 설문은 지어낸 거예요. 실제 거래는 회사와 확인하세요.
steps.blank:
A: Would you be ___ to send it to your users?   B: Only if it’s short. Let’s meet ___. Fifteen? 
A: OK. If ___ share the results, ___ you send it?   B: That’s a ___! 
낱말 상자: willing · halfway · we · could · deal
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 들어 두면 좋은 비즈니스 낱말 (참고): a supplier 공급 업체(회사에 부품을 파는 곳) · a bike dealer 자전거 판매상 / a competitor · a rival 같은 시장의 경쟁 회사, 경쟁자 / a bid 입찰(일을 따내려고 내는 가격) · an acquisition (회사) 인수 / a shareholder 주주 · a dispute 분쟁, 의견 다툼
- 표현 더 보기 (참고): There’s no magic formula. 딱 맞는 공식은 없어요. / The answers are dependent on the weather. 응답은 날씨에 따라 달라요. / 대니얼의 연구실과 설문은 지어낸 거예요. 실제 거래는 회사와 확인하세요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Would you be ___ to send it to your users? B: Only if it’s short. Let’s meet ___. Fifteen? / A: OK. If ___ share the results, ___ you send it? B: That’s a ___! / 낱말 상자: willing · halfway · we · could · deal
Go through every point in each tip box (for example every greeting with its time of day), one or two short sentences each, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: negotiate (협상하다), agreement (합의, 협정), client (고객, 거래처), export (수출하다), import (수입하다), investor (투자자), invest (투자하다), finance (재정, 금융; 자금을 대다), commission (수수료), maximum (최대(한)), commercial (상업적인, 영리의), demand (요구하다; 수요).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. After every two or three words, ask one tiny real question with the word you just did (for example: Are you a morning person?), wait for the answer and react; do this at least twice in this part. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: negotiation (협상) — "room for negotiation"; willing (기꺼이 ~하는) — "I’m willing to wait."; final (마지막의, 최종의) — "Is that your final offer?"; flexible (유연한, 융통성 있는) — "We can be flexible."; budget (예산) — "It’s over budget."; offer (제안, 제시안) — "That’s our best offer."; condition (조건) — "I have one condition."; term ((terms) (거래·계약) 조건) — "Let’s agree on the terms."; compromise (타협, 절충안) — "Fifteen is a good compromise.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Your friend wants Saturday, and you want Sunday. What do you say?
Let’s meet halfway. What if we ___ instead?
Ask a friend to help you move a sofa.
Would you be willing to help me on Saturday?
Make an offer to your friend.
If you can help me, I could ___.
Do you like asking for a lower price at markets? Why?
Yes, I do. / Not really. I ___.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Your friend wants Saturday, and you want Sunday. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Let’s meet halfway. What if we ___ instead?)
- "Ask a friend to help you move a sofa." (hint on screen: Would you be willing to help me on Saturday?)
- "Make an offer to your friend." (hint on screen: If you can help me, I could ___.)
- "Do you like asking for a lower price at markets? Why?" (hint on screen: Yes, I do. / Not really. I ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: Your friend wants Saturday, and you want Sunday. What do you say?
Ask a friend to help you move a sofa.
Make an offer to your friend.
Do you like asking for a lower price at markets? Why?

steps.title: Running It by Maya
steps.text: The next morning, Jiwoo *set off* early to talk to Maya. She explained the deal: fifteen questions, a mid-January deadline, results shared with the team first, and a free ride for each participant. Maya liked it. “There’s *no such* thing as a perfect survey, but this is a good one. It’s *by no means* a *large scale* study, but the output could help both sides.” She added two conditions: the survey must exclude names and phone numbers, and the lab can’t distribute the data to anyone else. A contract or a simple email? Maya chose *the latter* for now. Daniel replied in an hour: “I agree to *the above*. Let’s seal the deal with coffee!” He also hoped for a good ratio of weekday and weekend riders.
steps.gloss: set off 출발하다, 길을 나서다 · by no means 결코 ~ 아닌 · output 결과물 · exclude 빼다, 제외하다 · distribute 나눠 주다, 배포하다 · the latter (둘 중) 후자 · the above 위의 내용 · seal the deal 거래를 확정하다
questions: What two conditions did Maya add?
How did they put the deal in writing?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Running It by Maya". Text: "The next morning, Jiwoo set off early to talk to Maya. She explained the deal: fifteen questions, a mid-January deadline, results shared with the team first, and a free ride for each participant. Maya liked it. “There’s no such thing as a perfect survey, but this is a good one. It’s by no means a large scale study, but the output could help both sides.” She added two conditions: the survey must exclude names and phone numbers, and the lab can’t distribute the data to anyone else. A contract or a simple email? Maya chose the latter for now. Daniel replied in an hour: “I agree to the above. Let’s seal the deal with coffee!” He also hoped for a good ratio of weekday and weekend riders." Words: set off 출발하다, 길을 나서다 · by no means 결코 ~ 아닌 · output 결과물 · exclude 빼다, 제외하다 · distribute 나눠 주다, 배포하다 · the latter (둘 중) 후자 · the above 위의 내용 · seal the deal 거래를 확정하다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What two conditions did Maya add?" / "How did they put the deal in writing?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘Would you be willing to ___?’로 정중하게 부탁할 수 있어요.
‘If you can ___, we could ___.’로 조건을 걸어 제안할 수 있어요.
‘Let’s meet halfway.’로 서로 양보해 중간에서 맞추자고 할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Would you be willing to ___?’로 정중하게 부탁할 수 있어요.
- ‘If you can ___, we could ___.’로 조건을 걸어 제안할 수 있어요.
- ‘Let’s meet halfway.’로 서로 양보해 중간에서 맞추자고 할 수 있어요.
First ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence, and stop there to wait. React and praise specifically. Only then, in a later turn, end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

lessons.title: 뉴스 이야기
lessons.goal: 출처를 밝혀 소식을 전하고, 짐작을 말하고, 궁금한 점 말하기

steps.title: 뉴스 이야기
steps.goal: 출처를 밝혀 소식을 전하고, 짐작을 말하고, 궁금한 점 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 12월 중순 오후, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 대니얼이 태블릿을 지우 쪽으로 돌려 뉴스 목록(글자 없이 회색 줄과 작은 막대그래프만)을 보여 주고, 지우가 몸을 기울여 눈을 가늘게 뜨고 화면을 들여다봄. 탁자 위 커피잔 두 개, 창밖은 초겨울 거리(간판·화면에 글자 없이)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat, one question per turn: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally. The warm-up is long enough only when the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions (one is enough if your class notes say you already had a class with them today); do not mention today's topic or ask if they are ready before that.
2) Then, in a new turn, bring up today's topic in your own words: "According to this article…" (뉴스 이야기). Goal: 출처를 밝혀 소식을 전하고, 짐작을 말하고, 궁금한 점 말하기. Today's scene: 12월 중순 오후, 동네 카페 창가 자리. 대니얼이 태블릿을 지우 쪽으로 돌려 뉴스 목록을 보여 주고, 지우가 몸을 기울여 눈을 가늘게 뜨고 화면을 들여다봄. 탁자 위 커피잔 두 개, 창밖은 초겨울 거리. People in the scene (say the names exactly like this): Daniel, Jiwoo. Say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above). Bring up the topic only once and ask if they are ready only once. When the learner says they are ready, answer with one short, warm sentence like a person would (for example: Great, let's start.) and nothing more.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "According to ___, ___.".

steps.when: 정보가 어디서 나왔는지 밝혀요. *according to* 뒤에는 출처(기사, 뉴스, 전문가).
steps.extra: According to this article, the bus drivers are planning a strike.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "According to ___, ___." (~에 따르면, ~래요.). When to use it: 정보가 어디서 나왔는지 밝혀요. according to 뒤에는 출처(기사, 뉴스, 전문가). Note: According to this article, the bus drivers are planning a strike.
Teach it like a person, in three small turns. One thing per turn, and wait for the learner each time. Never name these turns or say what kind of practice comes next; just talk:
(1) Say it once inside a real everyday moment (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can) and let the learner say it.
(2) The learner says it with their own real word in the blank (for example their own name). Show it first with your own real word; nobody ever says the blank itself. Any word of theirs that makes a correct sentence is right, even when the book uses another one.
(3) Have a tiny real exchange with it, like in a normal conversation: ask the learner something that this expression answers, or let them say it to you, and give your own real answer (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way).
Fix at most one thing, gently, and only if it is really wrong. If you need a word for it, say this expression or this sentence. This expression is finished only when the learner has said it in three separate turns and you have replied to the last one. Then call next_step.

lines.en: {{Did you see the latest on}} the bus strike? It’s been in the news a lot lately.

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key sentences: According to ___, ___. / I wonder if ___. Table (출처 → 내용):
- this article → the bus drivers are planning a strike.
- the report → most riders are office workers.
- a recent survey → more people ride in spring.
- the news → the council will vote next month.
Make three quick real-life moments out of the key sentences and the rows, one per turn (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. If their sentence is correct and natural, accept it even when the table uses other words. Do not read labels or arrows aloud, and never say a blank: use real words. This part is finished only when the learner has answered three of these moments. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
*According to* the report, … 보고서에 따르면 …(출처) 
내 생각은: In my opinion, … 
*It seems (that)* trips went up. 이용이 늘어난 것 같아요(본 것을 바탕으로 한 짐작).

*I wonder if* it’s true. 사실인지 궁금해요. (if is it ×) 
*I wonder if* we could add a notice. 안내를 넣으면 어떨까 싶어요(부드러운 제안). 
I wonder *when* it will end. 언제 끝날지 궁금해요.
errors: I wonder if is it true.
내 생각을 말할 때는 according to를 쓰지 않아요.
According to the news says, it’s Friday.
According to the news, it’s Friday.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- According to … · It seems (that) …: According to the report, … 보고서에 따르면 …(출처) / 내 생각은: In my opinion, … / It seems (that) trips went up. 이용이 늘어난 것 같아요(본 것을 바탕으로 한 짐작).
- I wonder if + 평서문: I wonder if it’s true. 사실인지 궁금해요. (if is it ×) / I wonder if we could add a notice. 안내를 넣으면 어떨까 싶어요(부드러운 제안). / I wonder when it will end. 언제 끝날지 궁금해요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- I wonder if is it true. → I wonder if it’s true. (if 뒤에는 평서문 순서(it’s).)
- According to me, it’s good. → In my opinion, it’s good. (내 생각을 말할 때는 according to를 쓰지 않아요.)
- According to the news says, it’s Friday. → According to the news, it’s Friday. (출처 뒤에 says를 붙이지 않아요.)
There are 2 grammar points and 3 mistakes. Go through them as a conversation, one new thing per turn, never as a lecture. Start with the first point right away, with no opening sentence about how you will do this:
- Each grammar point: say its main idea in one or two plain, easy sentences with one short example with real words (do not go through every detail of the point), then ask the learner to make one short sentence of their own with it. When they answer, react to their sentence in a few words, and go on to the next thing in the same reply.
- Then the mistakes, one at a time: say the wrong sentence and ask the learner to fix it. When they answer, first confirm the right sentence and say why in a few words, then give the next wrong sentence in the same reply. Do every mistake on screen this way.
Never give two new points or two new mistakes in one turn, and never skip the confirmation. After the last mistake is fixed and confirmed, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: According to … · It seems (that) …: According to the report, … 보고서에 따르면 …(출처) 내 생각은: In my opinion, … It seems (that) trips went up. 이용이 늘어난 것 같아요(본 것을 바탕으로 한 짐작).
I wonder if + 평서문: I wonder if it’s true. 사실인지 궁금해요. (if is it ×) I wonder if we could add a notice. 안내를 넣으면 어떨까 싶어요(부드러운 제안). I wonder when it will end. 언제 끝날지 궁금해요.
mistakes: I wonder if is it true. → I wonder if it’s true.
According to me, it’s good. → In my opinion, it’s good.
According to the news says, it’s Friday. → According to the news, it’s Friday.

steps.note: 예) this article / a strike next Friday → According to this article, there’s a strike next Friday. — I wonder if the bikes will run out.
steps.teach:
Quick practice. How it works (written on the learner's screen; do not read it out): 예) this article / a strike next Friday → According to this article, there’s a strike next Friday. — I wonder if the bikes will run out. The items (the words the learner gets for each one): this article / a strike next Friday | the weather report / snow tomorrow | a recent survey / more riders in spring | the news / a new bike lane.
The sample on screen shows what is said for one item and who says it (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes it is a two-person exchange). If the sample has a dash (—), the words before the dash are one speaker and the words after it are the other: split it like a real conversation, the learner says one side and you say the other. The learner should get to use the given words. If both words belong to one side, the learner says that side and you say the other. If the words are split between the two sides (for example a question with the first word and an answer with the second), take turns across the items: for one item you ask and the learner answers with the second word, for the next the learner asks with the first word and you answer. When you set up an item, say which side the learner takes and give them only the word that goes into it. Never make the learner say both sides in one go. If their sentence is correct English and uses the given word, it is right: say so and go on, and never ask for extra words from the sample. Do not say the sample or the answer before the learner tries: from the first item they build it themselves. Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear, in different words each time, let the learner answer, and react like a person. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "According to this article…" (뉴스 이야기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "According to ___, ___." / "It seems (that) ___." / "I wonder if ___.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: It’s been in the news a lot lately.
Did you see the latest on ___?
It’s hard to tell if it’s true.
I’ll have to look into it.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 소식 전하기: "I read an article about ___." (~에 관한 기사를 읽었어요., 보통); "It was in the headlines." (주요 뉴스로 나왔어요., 보통); "The report says that ___." (보고서에 따르면 ~래요., 보통); "Experts say ___." (전문가들은 ~라고 해요., 보통); "It’s been in the news a lot lately." (요즘 뉴스에 많이 나와요., 보통); "Did you see the latest on ___?" (~ 최신 소식 봤어요?, 친근)
- 곰곰이 생각하기: "It’s hard to tell if it’s true." (사실인지 판단하기 어려워요., 보통); "I’ll have to look into it." (좀 더 알아봐야겠어요., 보통); "It makes you think." (생각해 보게 되네요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 머리기사 (수업용으로 지어낸 것)

City Council to Vote on New Bike Lanes 시의회, 새 자전거 도로 표결 예정

*political* 정치의, 정치적인 · *current affairs* 시사(요즘 중요한 뉴스)

A: Did you see the ___ on the bus strike?   B: Yes. According ___ this article, it’s next Friday. 
A: I wonder ___ the bikes will run out.   B: It’s hard to ___. I’ll have to look ___ it.

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 머리기사 (수업용으로 지어낸 것): City Council to Vote on New Bike Lanes 시의회, 새 자전거 도로 표결 예정 / Governor Visits Towns After Flood Disaster 주지사, 홍수 재해 뒤 마을 방문 / Minister Announces Child Welfare Plan 장관, 아동 복지 계획 발표 / Federal Agency Shares New Economy Statistics 연방 기관, 새 경제 통계 공개 / 머리기사는 작은 낱말을 빼요. to vote = will vote(표결할 예정)
- (참고) 뉴스 낱말 더 보기: political 정치의, 정치적인 · current affairs 시사(요즘 중요한 뉴스) / military 군대(의) · troops 병력, 군인들 · defense 국방, 방어 / a secretary (정부) 장관; 비서 · news coverage 보도, 취재 / a terrorist 테러범(정치적 목적으로 폭력을 쓰는 사람) · the establishment of ~의 설립
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Did you see the ___ on the bus strike? B: Yes. According ___ this article, it’s next Friday. / A: I wonder ___ the bikes will run out. B: It’s hard to ___. I’ll have to look ___ it. / 낱말 상자: latest · to · if · tell · into
Go through every point in each tip box (for example every greeting with its time of day), one or two short sentences each, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: article ((신문·인터넷) 기사), headline ((기사) 제목, 머리기사), journalist (기자), expert (전문가), survey (설문 조사), government (정부), election (선거), statistics (통계), press (언론, 기자단), vote (투표하다), council ((시) 의회), president (대통령).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. After every two or three words, ask one tiny real question with the word you just did (for example: Are you a morning person?), wait for the answer and react; do this at least twice in this part. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: research (연구) — "Daniel’s research is on bikes."; economy (경제) — "news about the economy"; official (공무원, 관리) — "a city official"; issue (문제, 쟁점) — "Safety is a big issue."; report (보고서) — "a new report"; source (출처) — "Is the source accurate?"; media (언론, 매체) — "The media covered it."; policy (정책) — "a new city policy"; recent (최근의) — "a recent survey".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Where do you usually get your news?
I usually read the news on ___. / I watch the news on TV.
Tell me about a news story you read recently.
I read an article about ___. According to it, ___.
What’s something you wonder about your city?
How can you tell if a news story is accurate?
I check the source. / I look for other reports.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Where do you usually get your news?" (hint on screen: I usually read the news on ___. / I watch the news on TV.)
- "Tell me about a news story you read recently." (hint on screen: I read an article about ___. According to it, ___.)
- "What’s something you wonder about your city?" (hint on screen: I wonder if ___.)
- "How can you tell if a news story is accurate?" (hint on screen: I check the source. / I look for other reports.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
